value.behaviour: Reproduces the startup crash with a real prepared app and pins bootstrap, finalization, compat and wiring-error behaviour of both useRouteRef hooks.
rules: Every new case sits in one new describe named 'useRouteRef during app bootstrap', so the red check `-t during.app.bootstrap` selects these cases and no others.

Fixture: `const pageRouteRef = createRouteRef()` and a frontend plugin 'test' with `routes: { page: pageRouteRef }` holding `PageBlueprint.make({ params: { path: '/target', routeRef: pageRouteRef, loader: async () =>
Target Page
} })`. Use the outer describe's `appPlugin`, which keeps that page behind app/root.children.
Root elements are `AppRootElementBlueprint.make({ name, params: { element } })` extensions of plugin 'test'. Call the core hook as `useCoreRouteRef(pageRouteRef as unknown as CoreRouteRef)`.

Capture errors with a module on plugin 'app' whose `ApiBlueprint.make` provides errorApiRef, shaped like the featureFlagsApiRef override at lines 1707-1714, with `{ post: jest.fn(), error$: jest.fn() } as unknown as typeof errorApiRef.T`. A local helper returns `post.mock.calls.map(([error]) => String(error))`.
Compare that helper's result to [] as the first bootstrap assertion, so on the unfixed code the test fails printing the `No path for` message (AC-1).

Render with `const { rerender } = render(preparedApp.getBootstrapApp().element)`. Finalize inside `await act(async () => { ... })`, assigning the result of `waitForFinalizedApp(preparedApp)` to a local, then call `rerender(finalizedApp.element)`. This is the swap PreparedAppRoot does in createApp.
Each element reports mounts from a `useEffect` with empty deps to a jest.fn, so a remount fails the test. The location stays at the jsdom default '/', and no case navigates.
Assert with `screen` and `findBy*`, in the file's `await expect(screen.findByText(...)).resolves.toBeInTheDocument()` style.

tests.name: keeps both hooks working from bootstrap through finalization
tests.given: an app with no sign-in page and two root elements: one calls the core hook and renders `<Link to={routeFunc()}>Core link</Link>` plus the text `Core route: ${routeFunc()}`, the other calls the frontend hook and renders `Frontend route: ${routeFunc?.() ?? 'none'}`
tests.expect: at bootstrap no error is posted, the texts are 'Core route: #' and 'Frontend route: none', and the link's href is '/'; after finalization both texts end in '/target', the href is '/target', and each element mounted exactly once

value.behaviour: Pins the core hook against a fake API carrying the lifecycle signal, and guards the legacy and signal-less behaviour that must not change.
rules: The reproducing case sits in a new describe named 'during app bootstrap', nested in the 'new app system' describe. The two guard cases sit outside it, so the red check judges the reproducing case only.

The fake API is `{ resolve, [Symbol.for('@backstage/frontend-plugin-api:route-resolution-lifecycle')]: { isFinalized, subscribe } }`. Spell the key out literally, because it pins the wire contract and U03's file does not exist when this test first runs. `subscribe` adds to a Set and returns a remover. A local `finalize()` sets the flag and calls the listeners.
Existing cases stay exactly as they are; only the listed sites change.
